name: The Grey Hourglass

rarity.note: Found where the Last God walked out; no craft of this world claims it.

summary: A glass hourglass held sideways in a frame of grey wood, found on the shore where Mornath was last seen walking out — the only object at the site, placed upright on a stone as if set down deliberately. Its sand does not fall. It moves only during Stilleven, the month of silence, flowing slowly from the left bulb to the right; after eight centuries it is perhaps a tenth shifted. Veil-Keepers tend its shrine and answer all questions about it with silence, which everyone agrees is appropriate.
origin: 1 Sun (winter's end) — found at the site of the Last God Walks
current_whereabouts: Its shrine beside the largest Stilleven vigil-ground in the Crownlands; tended by an unbroken succession of Veil-Keepers.
properties: Sand flows only during Stilleven — roughly a fistful per year, left to right
No one has determined what fills the right bulb when the left empties, or what happens then
The frame's grey wood matches no species on Aurelith
keepers: The Veil-Keepers by universal custom; every realm recognizes the shrine even where it recognizes nothing else of Mornath.
value_or_danger: Beyond transaction. The open question — what happens when the sand finishes — is the closest thing Aurelith has to a countdown.
adventure_hooks: This Stilleven, the sand moved two fistfuls. The Keepers have not announced it; players learn it anyway.
A Rememberer text claims the hourglass was Mornath's gift, not his leavings: 'he left the world his patience.' What it measures is not time.
